docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
GigaMeter Research Hub

The open-source telemetry research on internet connectivity, network quality, and physical location integrity across GigaMeter installed public facilities.

Spatial Intelligence

Models for entity geofencing, hardware mobility trajectories, and Wi-Fi spatial clustering.

Connectivity & Outages

Advanced telemetry models evaluating network uptime.

Network Diagnostics

NDT7 metric analysis to detect ISP throttling via bufferbloat latency and BBR capacity.

Decisions Data handling

docs.title: NNNN. Title
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted | Proposed | Superseded by NNNN
  • Date: YYYY-MM-DD
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: What is true today, and why a decision is needed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Write this section in the imperative. An ADR is Accepted only when the core decision is settled and matches the code. Anything open or unvalidated is Proposed. A settled ADR can still list a sub-question under Open questions; that sub-question is not decided.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: What follows from the decision, including what remains unchanged.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Omit this section when no alternative was real.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: Omit this section when nothing inside the ADR is undecided.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Repo files, functions, tests, or docs pages that were opened and checked. Label anything that comes from outside the repo as external and not verifiable here. Link related ADRs.

docs.title: 0001. Version the agent rules
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-18
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Agent rules lived only under gitignored .cursor/. The telemetry catalogue was applied to every chat, which spent context on field reference the docs are meant to hold.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Version only the slim, scrubbed rules under .cursor/rules/. Those files carry no internal names, IDs, URLs, credentials, or dated filenames. Leave the rest of .cursor/ ignored. Keep one short rule always on. Point SQL, ping, and NDT7 work at a docs data-dictionary page instead of sending the full catalogue into every chat. Commit the project rules. Do not publish them in MkDocs. An optional root AGENTS.md may point other agents at the same rules.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: .gitignore still ignores the whole .cursor/ directory, so the rules are not in git until that ignore is narrowed. The data-dictionary page is not written yet. Raw rule drafts stay off the published site.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Leaving the full telemetry catalogue always on kept the field list in every chat.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• .gitignore ignores .cursor/.
  • ADR 0007 is the public-repo constraint on what a versioned rule may contain.
  • The MkDocs configs under docs-site/ publish each site's docs/ directory only.

docs.title: 0002. MkDocs is the source of truth
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The methodology is written up in more than one place. Notebooks, chats, and dashboards drift from the write-up that was actually frozen.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Treat the versioned MkDocs site as the source of truth for methodology. Other tools hold notes only.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• README.md says the published documentation is the source of truth for how every result is computed.
  • docs-site/geofencing/mkdocs.yml builds the geofencing site and selects versions with mike.

docs.title: 0003. Versioning and freeze
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A code tag, the package version, and the published docs version can move separately. A wiring fix can ship without changing the method.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Tag releases git tag vX.Y.Z. Publish the docs with mike as a minor version vX.Y. Bump mike only at a freeze. Run scripts/replay_versions.py before every freeze, and keep replay outputs outside the repository. Record every method change in the Research Log.

A patch release does not get its own mike version. Docs stay on the minor, as in v0.3 for the v0.3.x tags.

The docs version is the Spatial Intelligence & Geofencing methodology version and appears as plain vX.Y in the version picker. The Outage and Routing pages are marked as unversioned drafts.

Keep pyproject.toml version equal to the release tag.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: Per-track sites and track-prefixed tags are proposed in ADR 0016. Existing tags v0.3.0, v0.3.1, and v0.3.2 stay as they are. pyproject.toml was left at 0.3.0.dev0 through v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 and set to 0.3.2 with tag v0.3.2.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• README.md, Versioning: geofencing docs are published with mike deploy --deploy-prefix geofencing --update-aliases --title "v0.3" v0.3 latest.
  • Research Log: status is frozen after replay validation. The "Operational-hours wiring" entry chooses no new version label.
  • scripts/replay_versions.py: outputs go to --out, default /tmp/gigameter-replay.
  • pyproject.toml: version = "0.3.2".

docs.title: 0004. SpatialConfig is the single source of numbers
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Methodology numbers were easy to copy into SQL, modules, and prose, and easy to treat as permanent once copied.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Keep methodology numbers only in SpatialConfig and on the Parameters page. Do not hard-code them. Do not treat the current values as permanent. Stamp outputs with methodology_version and config_hash.

Read operational_hours from that same config. It was the setting that broke this rule; v0.3.1 wires it back. See ADR 0011.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: The policy for versioning per-country overrides is not decided. workdays is one config value today, not resolved per country.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/spatial_intelligence/config.py: methodology_version is "0.3"; config_hash and provenance stamp outputs; with_overrides returns a validated copy.
  • Parameters: the same settings, with current value, status, and the version that set them.
  • tests/test_spatial_foundations.py: test_operational_hour_window_is_not_hard_coded_outside_config.
  • Research Log, "Operational-hours wiring". Tag v0.3.1.
  • Blueprint, Known Limitations: "Fixed workdays".

docs.title: 0005. One loader, one canonical frame
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Later stages were renaming columns and joining the schools table again. Two passes could disagree about the same facility.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Give TelemetryLoader.load exactly one source. Build db and delta_store from .env only when that source needs them. Canonicalise columns once, in the loader, and do not fall back to legacy telemetry names after that. Have FacilityValidator build fix events, device classes, and anchors once and pass them down. Do not alias identifiers or re-merge schools inside analyzers.

The column contract is ADR 0013. Pin ownership is ADR 0014.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/data_loader.py: load, _read_source (exactly one of frame, file, or query), _checked_db_connection, _delta_store_or_default, canonicalize_telemetry_columns.
  • tests/test_telemetry_loader.py: test_rejects_zero_or_two_sources, test_canonicalize_renames_aliases_once, test_facility_validator_reuses_spatial_summary.
  • src/spatial_intelligence/facility_validator.py builds one SpatialProfiler and passes its fix_event_rows into MobilityAnalyzer.
  • prepare_schools_frame still accepts giga_id_school on a schools table. Analyzer modules do not rename telemetry identifiers.

docs.title: 0006. Official pins come from Delta Sharing
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-18
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Location truth needs one official pin source. An earlier note asked for one live snapshot per run for every track.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Load official pins from Delta Sharing. The loader calls delta_store.load_table with the country code and renames that table's latitude and longitude to govt_latitude and govt_longitude. Who supplies pins at run time is ADR 0014.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
The "one live snapshot per run for all tracks" idea was narrowed on 2026-11-19. ADR 0014 leaves the app ingest workflow open, so one dashboard run can still mix two pin versions.

The name school_master is not in this repository. giga-spatial 0.11.1's load_table takes whatever table name the caller passes, and this repo passes the country code. Share and schema come from API_SHARE_NAME and API_SCHEMA_NAME.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/data_loader.py: prepare_schools_frame; _merge_school_pins calls store.load_table(country_iso3).
  • tests/test_telemetry_loader.py: test_delta_load_when_schools_df_omitted.
  • README.md, Configuration: Delta Sharing credentials and the share and schema variables.
  • gigaspatial/core/io/delta_sharing_data_store.py in giga-spatial 0.11.1: load_table(table_name).

docs.title: 0007. Public-repo data handling
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The repository is public. Ledgers contain facility and device identifiers, radio identifiers, and coordinates.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Do not put real school IDs, device IDs, SSIDs, BSSIDs, coordinates, or ledger country codes in code, tests, docs, pull requests, issues, or rules. Keep data/ local and gitignored. Use synthetic fixtures. Anonymise worked examples.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• README.md, Data Handling: data/, CSV, and Parquet stay gitignored; facility location is the Wi-Fi result only.
  • .gitignore ignores data/, *.csv, and *.parquet.
  • Worked Examples describe replayed cases without shipping a ledger.

docs.title: 0008. Schools only while on 0.x
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-18
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The GigaMeter app monitors schools, health facilities, and camps. This research line joins telemetry on a school id.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: While the project is on 0.x, cover schools only. Join on giga_id_school, which the loader canonicalises to school_id_giga. Revisit this before adding a health facility or a camp. Those entities break the assumption that the platform entity id is the school id.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/data_loader.py: TELEMETRY_COLUMN_ALIASES maps giga_id_school to school_id_giga; REQUIRED_TELEMETRY_COLUMNS requires school_id_giga.
  • sql/fetch_spatial_confidence_ledger.sql reads school.giga_id_school.
  • README.md describes the app's three entity types. The implemented spatial questions in this repo run on the school id.

docs.title: 0009. SQL conventions
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-18
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Track C queries are not in the repo yet. Three conventions need one place before the first of those queries. This ADR stays Proposed: the bandwidth and retransmission wording is not in the SQL, and the legacy-client coalesce is not validated.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Do not treat this ADR as implemented. Apply it with the first Track C query.

  1. Compare app versions as integer arrays, not as strings. This part is already in the ledger, coverage, and country queries.
  2. Report NDT7 BBR bandwidth as BBRInfo.BW in bytes/s × 8 / 1e6, in Mbps. Define retransmission ratio as BytesRetrans / BytesSent, and extract both fields. Do not call that ratio packet loss. This wording was set on 2026-11-18. The SQL does not do it yet.
  3. Queries that span app 2.x and older clients must coalesce the nested NDT7 paths with the flat NDT-5 keys. This part is unvalidated. Current NDT extraction reads only the nested NDT7 paths.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Traceroutes & BBR calls BBRInfo.BW bytes/sec and does not apply × 8. That page is frozen methodology, so this ADR does not edit it. The two statements disagree until a freeze adopts one.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• sql/fetch_spatial_confidence_ledger.sql compares app_version with integer arrays. The same predicate is in fetch_spatial_confidence_ledger_all.sql, fetch_spatial_telemetry_coverage.sql, and fetch_countries_with_coordinates.sql.
  • Research Log, "Code Defects Found in v0.2": a string comparison sorted 2.0.10 below 2.0.2.
  • sql/fetch_measurements.sql and sql/fetch_measurements_utc.sql store $["NDTResult.S2C"].LastServerMeasurement.BBRInfo.BW as a raw double, bbr_bottleneck_bw, and TCPInfo.TotalRetrans as tcp_total_retrans. They do not select BytesRetrans or BytesSent, and they do not read flat NDT-5 keys.
  • sql/fetch_measurements.sql has no app_version filter. Whether a future Track C query excludes older clients before the coalesce is still open.

docs.title: 0010. Python and dependencies
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The spatial code has to run on the interpreters that are actually tested. Pandas 3 changed groupby, and a loader bug showed up only there.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Support Python ≥ 3.10 and pandas 2.3 and 3.0. Run the tests on both. Take shared distance helpers from giga-spatial. Other helpers in src/spatial_intelligence/geo.py may move there.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: One test is unaccounted for between Python 3.10 (115 passed) and Python 3.14 (113 passed, 1 skipped). That count is external and was not investigated here. No CI workflow in this repo runs the matrix.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.10", pandas>=2.3,<4, giga-spatial>=0.9.8.
  • README.md: Python 3.10 or newer.
  • src/spatial_intelligence/geo.py: haversine_m calls gigaspatial.processing.calculate_distance. Weighted centroids and the DBSCAN wrapper still live in that module.
  • Research Log: TelemetryLoader lost tz_name under pandas 3; the time zone is now mapped per facility.
  • No .github workflow is in the repository.

docs.title: 0011. Operational hours are applied from SpatialConfig
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Local time is created_timestamp converted at the facility. That conversion does not decide which hours count.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Apply the window from SpatialConfig.

SpatialConfig.operational_hours is an inclusive pair of integer local hours, and the end hour covers HH:00–HH:59. in_operational_hours is the only comparison. A fix event keeps the flag from its first row, so a burst that starts inside the window and finishes outside it stays in the anchor window. Governance percentages, the hourly chart, and the BSSID split count every row and do not apply the workday filter. An overnight window is rejected.

(8, 19) means 08:00:00–19:59:59. The anchor requires both is_workday and is_operational_hours. The profiler recomputes the flag per row from local_hour only. The enricher does not write the flag. methodology_version stays "0.3".

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: Which timestamp is the real test time for a row synced after the device was offline is unresolved. See ADR 0015.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/spatial_intelligence/config.py: default (8, 19); __post_init__ requires integers 0–23, rejects bools, requires start ≤ end, and rejects an overnight window; in_operational_hours is the comparison.
  • src/spatial_intelligence/fix_events.py: mark_fix_events recomputes the flag and logs one warning when an incoming stamp disagrees; build_fix_event_table takes is_operational_hours with "first".
  • src/spatial_intelligence/spatial_profiler.py: _apply_operational_hours; _anchor_window_events requires is_workday and is_operational_hours. Governance and BSSID counts sum the recomputed flag across rows.
  • tabs/tab_01_governance.py: the hourly chart groups every row by local_hour and is_operational_hours.
  • src/utils/timezone_enricher.py does not write is_operational_hours.
  • tests/test_spatial_foundations.py: test_recomputed_operational_hours_replace_a_disagreeing_stamp, test_burst_crossing_the_end_hour_stays_in_window_from_its_first_row, test_operational_hour_window_is_not_hard_coded_outside_config (the hard-coded BETWEEN 8 AND 19 form is rejected outside config), test_measurement_sql_does_not_stamp_operational_hours.
  • tests/test_spatial_profiler.py: test_anchor_window_requires_workday_and_operational_hours_flags.
  • Research Log, "Operational-hours wiring".

docs.title: 0012. Time basis
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0011 applies the hour window to local time. The clock that produces that local time has to be the facility, because a device clock and an IP time zone follow the handset or the ISP.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Derive local time from created_timestamp (backend created_at, UTC), converted at the facility. Resolve the zone from the official pin, then the detected coordinates, then the country's first listed zone, then UTC. Do not use the device clock. Do not use client_info.Timezone. Keep the first-listed-zone fallback as it is. It is defensive.

Treat created_at as the backend write time, in UTC, and as the timestamp closest to the test. Treat scheduled_at as the time the test request was sent. The device may be off then. It is not the test time.

Leave ping cadence at 15 minutes. A row that waited in the offline queue carries its sync or write time, so local_hour and the local date can be wrong. From app 2.0.4, offline_synced is meant to flag those rows. On earlier rows the flag is not a reliable test of queueing. What to do about the queued rows is ADR 0015.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: sql/fetch_spatial_confidence_ledger.sql stores created_at as created_timestamp and does not convert it. The loader does. sql/fetch_measurements.sql converts with default.country_timezones (COALESCE of that table, a country-name match, then UTC). That is not the pin cascade above.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Using client_info.Timezone was the old rule. IP zones follow ISP hubs and VPNs, so it is obsolete.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: The research window, 08:00–19:59 facility-local, differs from an 8am–4pm window in the analytics tables. That is a communication question, not a code change. The analytics window is not described in this repository.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/timezone_enricher.py: _resolve_single_school_tz checks govt_latitude / govt_longitude, then detected_latitude / detected_longitude, then pytz.country_timezones index 0, then "UTC". enrich_telemetry_with_local_time parses created_timestamp into created_timestamp_utc and converts that. It does not read a device clock or client_info.
  • tests/test_spatial_foundations.py: test_enrichment_keeps_tz_name_and_converts_each_timezone.
  • External, not verifiable in this repo (app engineering team, 2026-11-19): created_at is the closest write time; scheduled_at is only the request time; cadence is 15 minutes on Windows 2.0.4, the Chrome extension, and Android; offline_synced is the 2.0.4 queue flag. Whether earlier rows store null or a default false is unverified. The app's own ping schedule is not in this repo.

docs.title: 0013. Canonical frame contract
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0005 canonicalises once. "Required" was easy to misread as "non-null", which would drop older rows and unresolved Wi-Fi lookups.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
After canonicalisation, require school_id_giga, device_id, detected_latitude, detected_longitude, and created_timestamp. Required means the column is present. It does not mean the values are non-null.

Keep rows with a null device_id. The SQL always selects it, and older app versions leave it empty. Never drop those rows for the null. Keep null detected coordinates in the frame. Spatial classes drop those rows later. Do not impute them, and do not take them from IP coordinates. Leave a missing pin null.

Pass a fully enriched frame through unchanged when both local_created_timestamp and local_hour are present and neither contains nulls. Raise ValueError when local time is only partly present, or when either column contains nulls.

Do not make is_operational_hours a loader column. See ADR 0011. The column table is on the Data Loading page.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: Rows without a device_id skip the device step. MobilityAnalyzer visits each device_id from unique(), and a null does not match any row, so those rows are not classified. The v0.4 path for them is undefined.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/data_loader.py: REQUIRED_TELEMETRY_COLUMNS; _clock_is_complete raises on a partial clock or on nulls, and returns false when both clock columns are absent; _require_columns checks presence only.
  • tests/test_telemetry_loader.py: test_partial_or_null_local_time_raises, test_skips_clients_when_frame_is_already_enriched.
  • Data Loading: nullable device_id, null detected coordinates, and no IP fill.
  • Blueprint, Data Dictionary Rules: missing device_id still counts as facility evidence and is left out of device mobility. spatial_profiler._unique_values drops nulls before the device-id list. pandas.Series.nunique does not count them.
  • src/spatial_intelligence/mobility_analyzer.py: analyze_device_mobility filters with device_id == device_id. On pandas 2.3.3 that comparison matches no row when the id is null, and the call returns an error.

docs.title: 0014. Pin ownership
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Official pins can arrive on an enriched frame, on a caller-supplied schools table, or from Delta Sharing. The loader has to pick one source. The dashboard also loads a second table for Track 3. See ADR 0006.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
TelemetryLoader owns pins. The class has to work for any caller, and a ledger is a frozen input.

On a frame whose local time is already complete, accept the govt pins already on it and do not call Delta. Non-null govt_latitude / govt_longitude are the usual case, for example an enriched ledger. If schools_df is also passed, only cross-check, by haversine distance. Raise ValueError when a pin is more than PIN_MATCH_M (1 m) away, or when the frame pin is null and schools_df has a coordinate for that facility. Do not treat these as mismatches: a facility missing from one side, extra rows, a null coordinate in schools_df, or both sides null.

On a frame that still needs local time, take pins from schools_df, then from non-null govt columns, then from Delta via the country code. All-null govt columns count as missing. If none of those sources exist, raise.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
The app ingest workflow is not settled.

app.py load_live_pins pulls live Delta Sharing pins, on unless GIGAMETER_LIVE_PINS=0, and passes them only as Track 3 entity_pins. Tracks 1 and 2 keep the ledger pins. One dashboard run can mix two pin versions.

Fix that by redesigning the app's ingest workflow, not by patching the toggle. One example, not a decision: refresh pins at ingest through the loader and record the Delta snapshot date.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• src/utils/data_loader.py: _clock_is_complete chooses the enriched branch; _reject_pin_mismatch and _differing_facility_count implement the 1 m and null-frame rules; _merge_school_pins is the non-enriched order; PIN_MATCH_M = 1.0. The enriched branch keys off a complete clock, including a frame whose govt pins are null, and still does not call Delta unless schools_df is passed.
  • tests/test_telemetry_loader.py: test_enriched_frame_is_reused_with_or_without_a_country_code, test_enriched_matching_schools_df_keeps_frame_pins, test_enriched_schools_df_mismatch_raises, test_enriched_null_frame_pin_against_schools_df_raises, test_enriched_subset_schools_df_leaves_other_pins, test_schools_df_merge_does_not_call_delta, test_existing_govt_pins_skip_delta_on_query_path, test_all_null_govt_columns_with_country_code_load_delta, test_missing_pin_source_raises.
  • app.py: LIVE_PINS_DEFAULT and load_live_pins; build_engine passes those pins only as entity_pins. src/spatial_intelligence/facility_validator.py uses entity_pins for Track 3 and leaves the telemetry govt columns on the frame used for Tracks 1 and 2.

docs.title: 0015. Test timestamp for offline-synced rows
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR 0012 turns created_at into local time. A row that sat in the offline queue carries write time, so its local hour can fall outside the window that the test actually ran in. Changing the clock is a methodology change for v0.4, not a patch. Roadmap priority P3.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Do not adopt this yet. The candidate is:

test_timestamp_utc = COALESCE(NDT S2C StartTime, created_at), plus a test_time_source flag.

Derive local time from test_timestamp_utc. Keep created_at as the write time.

StartTime is the M-Lab server timestamp in UTC, at $["NDTResult.S2C"].LastServerMeasurement.ConnectionInfo.StartTime in results.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Accept this only after replaying tag v0.3.1 against the candidate and counting changed anchor events. Whether created_at itself changes when a queued row syncs is unverified.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• sql/fetch_measurements.sql does not extract ConnectionInfo.StartTime.
  • External, not verifiable in this repo. One anonymised country, created_at from January through March 2026:
  • StartTime is present on about 90–97% of rows from app 1.0.9, and on none before that.
  • The lag from StartTime to created_at has a median of 22–24 s on every version. The 95th percentile is 28–45 s.
  • Only app 2.0.3 has a long tail: 99th percentile 2,336 s, mean 1,712 s.
  • The gain is mainly that 2.0.3 offline tail.

docs.title: 0016. Per-track documentation sites and versions
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-21
  • Deciders: Utku Can Ozturk

docs.title: Context
docs.text: One mike version covers the whole site. Geofencing is at v0.3. Outage and routing are unversioned drafts. A second released track cannot have its own version while sharing that picker.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Publish an unversioned landing site at the root. It carries the hero, the track cards, Decisions, and data handling.

Give each track its own MkDocs config under docs-site/. Shared theme, palette, and markdown extensions live in docs-site/base.yml. Path-based settings stay in the track config, because INHERIT does not rewrite paths.

Version geofencing with mike and --deploy-prefix geofencing. versions.json lives at geofencing/versions.json. The published minors are v0.2 and v0.3, with latest as the alias of v0.3. The picker title is plain vX.Y. Every mike command includes --deploy-prefix. There must never be a versions.json at the site root: an unversioned track requests that file, and a root file would show another track's versions.

Leave outage and routing as unversioned plain builds until each reaches v0.1. Their configs already set extra.version.provider: mike and a deploy prefix, so a later mike deploy --deploy-prefix outage does not share geofencing's version list.

From the next release onward, tag tracks geofencing-vX.Y.Z, outage-vX.Y.Z, and routing-vX.Y.Z. Leave the existing tags v0.3.0, v0.3.1, and v0.3.2 as they are. Do not retag them. Keep pyproject.toml version as the package version.

Keep links inside one site relative, so they stay on that version. Point links that cross sites at root-absolute paths such as /gigameter-research/adr/... and /gigameter-research/geofencing/latest/....

Redirect the old /v0.2/, /v0.3/, and /latest/ URLs with scripts/redirect_legacy_docs.py. Geofencing pages go to /geofencing/<version>/.... Decision pages go to /adr/.... Outage and routing pages go to their unversioned sites.

Publish from a worktree of gh-pages. scripts/docs.sh migrate-gh-pages is the one-time move. scripts/docs.sh publish updates one site at a time. Do not use mkdocs gh-deploy; it replaces the branch and would wipe the geofencing tree mike deployed. The scripts commit locally and print git push origin gh-pages instead of pushing.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Search is per site. There is no cross-site search.

The version picker stays in the header. Material appends it to .md-header__topic from JavaScript. Moving it into the left nav is not a small partial override, so it is not done here.

A plain mkdocs build of a versioned track does not fill the picker. Publish geofencing with mike. mike set-default runs under the geofencing prefix, so the site root stays the landing page.

The copied v0.2 HTML is the already published build. It is not rebuilt from current sources.

docs/api and docs/adr remain symlinks to the geofencing API pages and the landing decisions, so the API doc test and the agent rules still resolve.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
Keeping one site and one picker until a second track releases. Rejected because the landing page, the shared decisions, and the track versions would stay tied together.

Rebuilding v0.2 from the current sources and labeling it v0.2. Rejected because those pages would no longer be the frozen build.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• docs-site/base.yml and docs-site/{landing,geofencing,outage,routing}/mkdocs.yml.
  • README.md, Versioning: mike deploy -f docs-site/geofencing/mkdocs.yml --deploy-prefix geofencing --update-aliases --title "v0.3" v0.3 latest.
  • ADR 0003: the open question points here. Tags v0.3.0, v0.3.1, and v0.3.2 are unchanged.
  • scripts/docs.sh: migrate-gh-pages and publish commit on the pages branch and do not push. scripts/redirect_legacy_docs.py writes the legacy refresh stubs.
  • pyproject.toml: version = "0.3.2".
